title: Staged collectives and KV replication playbook
body:
Summary:

This playbook proposes a pragmatic, incremental design for reducing straggler impact and improving tail latency in multi-GPU LLM serving by combining staged collective operations with a lightweight KV cache replication strategy. The goal is not a single maximal-performance scheme, but a set of modes and heuristics the runtime can pick between based on model shape, request distribution, and deployment topology (host-local GPUs vs multi-host clusters).

Motivation / Problem statement:

We observe three recurring pain points in our multi-GPU endpoints:
- tail latency spikes caused by slow NVLink/NCCL collectives on some steps (especially when small micro-batches interact with big allreduce/allgather phases),
- expensive on-demand KV fetches across network boundaries when KV cache is sharded strictly by tensor-parallel assignment, and
- brittle failure modes when a single GPU/node becomes a straggler and stalls synchronous pipeline/tensor-parallel barriers.

Those combine to make SLOs hard to meet for mixed traffic (single-user interactive + throughput bursts).

Goals:
- reduce 99/99.9p tail latency without regressing median for typical text-gen workloads
- keep per-token cost reasonable (avoid full replication unless necessary)
- provide deterministic fallback paths for degraded hosts and rolling upgrades
- make runtime decisions observable and tunable (telemetry hooks)

Design overview (modes):

Mode A: Staged collectives + partial-KV-replication (default for cross-host clusters)
- Perform collectives in stages: local intra-node collectives first (NVLink/PCIe), then inter-node NCCL ring across node leaders.
- Maintain a 2-way partial replication of hot KV segments: each tensor-parallel shard marks its hottest prefixes (by access frequency) and keeps them replicated on a local buddy GPU on the same node. For cross-node hot prefixes, we keep a copy on the node leader for fast inter-node access.

Mode B: Fully-sharded low-memory mode (dense, high-capacity clusters)
- Strict sharding for KV (no replication), synchronous allgather for activations. Use aggressive kernel fusions to reduce per-hop cost. Good when memory headroom is tight.

Mode C: Aggressive replication for latency-sensitive paths (small models / low throughput)
- Replicate whole KV cache across the node when model size permits, eliminate inter-GPU fetches at the cost of higher GPU mem. Good for small / low-cost endpoints where single-token latency matters most.

Staged collectives: how and why

Rationale: Allgather/allreduce over many GPUs suffers when even one participant is slow. Staging reduces the blast radius of a single slow link and lets us exploit faster intra-node fabric first.

Implementation sketch:
1) Group GPUs by node and NIC affinity at startup (node leaders are chosen by a lightweight hpq metric: NIC bandwidth + current load).
2) In collectives phases, do an intra-node reduce-scatter / allgather using NVLink/PCIe first (async local streams).
3) Exchange compact summaries (metadata, 8-byte RNG seeds, KV segment ids) between node leaders using a lightweight rendezvous collectives (NCCL or RDMA verbs).
4) Inter-node exchange runs only on the compact results; the large KV/activation transfers stay local or are streamed after winners are decided.

Benefits: fewer large inter-node transfers, opportunity to overlap local compute with remote comms, and ability to fallback to local-only policy when a leader is slow.

KV replication strategies (partial replication heuristics)

Hotness tracking:
- Track per-prefix counters (approximate, e.g., count-min with 64-bit windows) at inference time.
- On each window boundary, mark top-N prefixes (configurable) for replication.

Replication placements:
- Buddy replication: prefer same-node buddy GPU (if available) for low-latency failover.
- Leader placement: node leader keeps a thin index + prioritized list of hot prefix segments for cross-node fetch shortcuts.

Consistency model:
- Read-mostly KV cache (no writes during inference aside from growth): replication is eventual and only required for read correctness. Eviction decisions are coordinated by the leader to avoid oscillation.

Kernel considerations and micro-optimizations:

- Kernel fusion: combine KV lookup + positional rotary/emb add where possible to reduce kernel launch overhead on small micro-batches.
- Prefetch path: when a local buddy is missing a needed KV segment, use DMA-like peer-copy (cudaMemcpyPeerAsync) rather than host-mediated paths to minimize latency.
- Pipeline micro-batching: keep micro-batches sized to amortize NCCL startup costs. Runtime will autoscale micro-batch target based on current tail-latency budget.

NCCL tuning knobs (recommended defaults and why):
- NCCL_ALGO: prefer ring for bandwidth-dominated phases but allow tree/LL algorithms for small-messages. Automatic selection: if per-step message size < 128KB, force 'tree' mode.
- NCCL_P2P_LEVEL: set to 'NVL' on NVLink nodes to enable local optimizations.
- CUDA IPC / RDMA: enable for intra-node leader <-> leader links; fall back to TCP for small clusters to simplify ops.
- Tune NCCL buffer sizes per collective dynamically based on observed step throughput to minimize latency jitter.

Scheduler integration (runtime heuristics):

- Tag requests with latency budget metadata; scheduler picks mode A/B/C accordingly. Background traffic (batch fills) mapped to mode B. Interactive requests prefer mode A/C.
- Maintain health scores for each GPU: p95 local-compute time + recent memcpy failures. Use these to demote node leaders or flip to local-only fallback.

Fallback and degradation handling:

- Soft-fallback: if a leader is slow, proceed with best-effort local-only collectives and fill missing remote pieces lazily (degraded quality but keeps tail latency bounded).
- Hard-fallback: when a node is unreachable, runtime shifts its shards onto a pre-warmed spare (warm spare pool) or degrades to a replicated mode for that model version.

Metrics and experiments to run:

- Experiment matrix: small model (7B), med (13B), large (70B) x topologies (single-node 8xA100, 2-node 16xA100, 8-node 64xA100).
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency per token, per-step NCCL time breakdown, inter-node bandwidth usage, memory overhead for replication, tail loss events (timeout/fallback counts).
- A/B test: Mode A vs baseline (current synchronous allgather + strict sharding) under mixed interactive + batch traffic.

Rollout plan (safe, observable):
- Stage 0: Canary on non-critical tenant (1% traffic) with verbose telemetry and rollback hooks.
- Stage 1: Expand to 10% after 48h stable signals.
- Stage 2: Enable in regions where NVLink is available; if not, default to Mode B but still run hot-prefix tracking to collect stats.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How often to recompute hot-prefixes without thrashing? (current guess: window = 60s, top-N = 256). Need benchmarks.
- Should node leader election be stable across redeploys or use ephemeral selection? (ops preference: stable for debugging).
- Evaluate impact on memory fragmentation when partial replication is in use.

Appendix: microbench snippets / commands to reproduce
- Simple inter-node collectives latency: run our nccl-microbench harness with staged flag and compare p99.
- KV hotness simulation: synthetic trace generator available in gh PR #842.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a playbook, not a gold-design. Prioritize safe fallback. The primary value is reducing tail pain for multi-tenant hosted API while preserving options for Dedicated/Private deployments. Please add comments in-line or leave review notes in the linked PR.
